A1.justification: Both complete, readable 49-page PDFs describe SimulCost. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated results.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM and optimization-baseline evaluations, simulation costs, ablations, statistical analyses, and failure traces.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulation and LLM evaluation results, with revised aggregates and statistical analyses alongside the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 extends the specified multi-round procedure with a nested branch: choose beta or k, then refine the inner spatial-resolution parameter until convergence. v2 explicitly classifies these coefficients as single-round-only. The core solver-interaction framework and search algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: CGYRO's gyrokinetic simulation coverage, comprising 31 tasks across 12 plasma profiles, is removed. EPOCH remains, reported separately. Hasegawa–Mima multi-round results already appear in v2, so their revised eligibility entries do not establish newly added solver coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 19 compares BO-GP with LLMs on EPOCH efficiency. That comparison disappears from v3 Table 19 and is not restored in the separate EPOCH tables. The comparator sets for retained analytical-solvers and classical-optimization experiments otherwise remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 changes the population underlying all main aggregates by excluding EPOCH and removing CGYRO. Table 2 also revises multi-round eligibility and counts, including Burgers 255→339 and Euler 148→197. Reported analytical-suite totals become 2,643 single-round and 2,304 multi-round tasks, with EPOCH separate. Some revisions correct documentation, since v2 already contains Hasegawa–Mima multi-round scores; reruns are not established.

E4.justification: Appendix B.6 replaces the pooled Euler beta-bias example with model-specific evidence across Euler and Burgers and adds quantified k-bias. The dataset-dependence robustness analysis is revised, while Table 9 drops reasoning-effort-specific fits. The ICL, reasoning-effort, prompt-sensitivity, and tool-augmented ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix C.3 and Table 9 change the reported estimator from mixed-effects logistic regression to a random-intercept linear probability model. McNemar testing, Benjamini–Hochberg correction, and Fisher-transformed correlation analysis remain. No increase in repeated runs or seeds is reported.

E6.justification: The headline estimates and comparative results are materially revised under the changed aggregate scope. GPT-5 single-round success changes from 65.0% to 61.5%; its multi-round efficiency changes from 0.57 to 0.66, versus GPT-OSS's 0.86→0.67, substantially narrowing their efficiency gap. Group statistics and statistical results also change. CGYRO results disappear; EPOCH scores are relocated unchanged. These are not same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: Removing the CGYRO subsection in Appendix A.2 also removes its gyrokinetic evolution equation and strong-magnetization/scale-separation assumptions. The retained solver mathematics, benchmark cost definitions, and Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion narrow the contribution from 13 simulators with broadly claimed platform-independent costs to 12 simulators, with main results restricted to 11 analytical-cost solvers and EPOCH separate. The central cost-aware benchmarking contribution and conclusions about unreliable guesses and inefficient trial-and-error remain.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 withdraws v2's inference that near-zero random-effect variance validates independence. v3 explains singular boundary estimates, weak identification with 11 datasets, and the distinction between failing to detect variation and establishing its absence. New Section C.15 also explicitly limits the scope of pooled cost comparisons.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 removes CGYRO's implementation link, discretization description, tuning details, and profile construction information. Section C.15 newly explains that Qwen3-32B was not evaluated on EPOCH. Hardware specifications, main hyperparameters, prompt examples, and the shared repository URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Lyu et al. (2025), distinguishing adaptive decisions about whether to invoke tools from cost-sensitive parameter tuning, and removes Candy et al. (2016) with CGYRO. BioML-bench's changed author attribution and numerous other reference edits concern existing works rather than added research coverage.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. Local revisions explain nested tuning and aggregate scope, rewrite the statistical interpretation, add Appendix C.15, correct references and cross-references, and replace the suppressed running title and preprint notice with publication formatting.

P2.justification: Figure 1 removes CGYRO, Table 2 separates analytical and wall-clock solvers, and EPOCH rows move from Tables 30–31 into Tables 32–33. Correlation matrices shrink from 25 to 19 parameters, and appendix figures and tables are repositioned. The overall visual design remains.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reporting accuracy by making the analytical-cost scope explicit, withdrawing the unsupported independence inference in Appendix C.3, and correcting the nonsignificant-model label to Claude in Table 10. Its mixed-accuracy ICL summary also now matches the retained Table 23. These gains are limited by largely unchanged empirical evidence and the loss of CGYRO coverage and the EPOCH–BO comparison.
